job.title: Financial Controller
job.description:
Hunter Manning is proud to be partnering with a highly successful Privately Owned Perth based business focused in the Construction & Engineering industry. Located south of the river in Perth, with a turnover exceeding $50 million and a strong trajectory for continued growth, this is a unique opportunity to join a business at a transformative time of strategic change and operational improvement.

The Opportunity:

Reporting directly to an exceptional CFO, the Financial Controller will play a pivotal role in shaping the financial operations of the business. This is more than a traditional FC role — it's an opportunity to drive continuous improvement, support business transformation, and provide meaningful insights that influence decision-making at the highest level.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Lead the day-to-day financial management, including month-end, compliance, and reporting.
  • Oversee the preparation of statutory accounts and liaise with external auditors.
  • Partner with operational teams to deliver financial insights and improve performance.
  • Enhance systems, processes, and controls in line with growth and best practice.
  • Support strategic initiatives, forecasting, and budgeting processes.


About You:

We are seeking a commerciall astute FC with broad experience and exposure to projects. You will be CPA or CA qualified with a strong foundation in financial reporting, compliance, and team leadership. Experience in a dynamic, fast-paced environment –

What’s on Offer:

  • Work alongside a high-calibre CFO with a track record of developing talent.
  • Be part of a listed business at a critical and exciting point of change.
  • A clear pathway to progress as the business continues to grow.
  • Competitive salary package and a collaborative, forward-thinking culture.

job.title: In-house lawyer - Commercial and Contracts
job.description:
We are partnering with an established mining services business in Perth to recruit an In-house Lawyer - Commercial and Contracts.

This is an excellent opportunity for a commercially minded lawyer who enjoys working closely with the business, providing practical advice and taking ownership of a broad range of legal and contractual matters.

Working as part of a collaborative legal and commercial function, you will support operational teams and senior stakeholders across contract negotiations, tenders, commercial risk and dispute resolution.

The role offers genuine autonomy, exposure to a diverse range of commercial matters and the opportunity to make a tangible impact on business outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

  • Draft, review and negotiate a broad range of commercial agreements, including customer contracts, master services agreements, subcontracts and supplier agreements.
  • Provide legal and commercial support on tenders, major proposals and contract negotiations.
  • Review contractual terms, identify key risks and recommend commercially practical solutions.
  • Advise on contract variations, pricing adjustments, contractual obligations and performance issues.
  • Support the management and resolution of commercial disputes, claims and contractual matters.
  • Partner with operational managers and senior stakeholders to provide clear, timely and commercially focused legal advice.
  • Assist with the development and improvement of contracting processes, templates and risk management practices.
  • Liaise with external legal advisers where specialist support is required.

About You We are looking for a pragmatic, commercially astute lawyer who can balance legal risk with operational and commercial objectives.
Ideally, you will bring:

  • A law degree and admission to practice in Australia. If you do not have a Law degree, extensive experience in Contracts may be suitable.
  • Experience in commercial contracts, either within private practice or an in-house legal environment.
  • Exposure to mining, mining services, construction, engineering, infrastructure or another contracting-intensive industry.
  • Strong experience drafting, reviewing and negotiating commercial agreements.
  • An understanding of contractual risk allocation, tender processes and commercial negotiations.
  • Confidence working directly with operational teams and senior stakeholders.
  • Excellent communication, negotiation and stakeholder management skills.
  • The ability to work autonomously, manage competing priorities and provide practical, solutions-focused advice.

Previous in-house experience would be advantageous, although lawyers from private practice with relevant commercial contracting experience are encouraged to apply.

What's on Offer?

  • A broad and varied in-house legal position with genuine responsibility.
  • Direct exposure to operational and commercial decision-making.
  • The opportunity to work on complex contracts and commercially significant matters.
  • A supportive and collaborative team environment.
  • Professional development and longer-term career opportunities.
  • A Perth-based role within an established mining services business.

job.title: AP Officer | Temp

job.title: FP&A Manager
job.description:
About the business
Our client is a privately owned mining services provider based near the airport with a strong National and International customer base. The business is seeking an FP&A Manager to join its finance function.

About the role

Reporting to the CFO, you'll turn operational activity into short-term and multi-year financial plans and give the business the insight it needs to make sound decisions. This is a hands-on leadership role where you'll work with senior management, operational leaders and the broader finance team.

Key responsibilities include:

  • Leading the annual budgeting process and preparing budget packs and commentary for senior management and the Board
  • Maintaining a rolling forecast, with variance analysis and clear commentary
  • Developing scenario and sensitivity models to support strategic and commercial decisions
  • Owning the standard cost framework and unit economics, including return on capital analysis
  • Producing monthly performance and cost analysis, identifying key drivers, risks and opportunities
  • Owning and improving the business's financial models and planning tools, including identifying opportunities to automate and streamline processes
  • Maintaining the integrity of planning and forecasting data in partnership with IT and operations
  • Contributing to monthly management and Board reporting
  • Leading, guiding and reviewing the work of a commercial analyst

About you

  • CPA or CA qualified
  • Solid experience in FP&A, management accounting or commercial finance
  • Advanced Excel skills and the ability to build financial models from scratch
  • Strong understanding of standard costing and variance analysis
  • Excellent communication skills and the confidence to present financial information to non-finance audiences
  • Collaborative, solutions-focused and able to manage competing priorities
  • Team leadership experience and experience in asset-intensive industries will be highly regarded

job.title: Assistant Accountant
job.description:
Hunter Manning is partnering with a well-established Australian business to recruit an Assistant Management Accountant who is looking for more than a traditional accounting role.

This is an opportunity to join a supportive and collaborative finance team within an established, operationally focused business. You'll be part of an environment where people are encouraged to contribute ideas, develop their skills and make a genuine impact.

Rather than being confined to traditional accounting responsibilities, you'll gain broad exposure to management reporting, costing, budgeting, forecasting and commercial analysis, while developing your skills in a role that directly supports business decision-making.

The Opportunity You'll join a friendly, hands-on finance team and play an important role in supporting management reporting, costing, budgeting, forecasting and operational performance analysis.

Working closely with senior finance leaders and operational stakeholders, you'll help analyse costs, business performance and key commercial drivers while providing meaningful insights to support strategic and operational decisions.
No two days will look quite the same, and you'll have plenty of opportunities to get involved in projects, process improvements and business initiatives that genuinely add value.

You'll also play an important role in improving Excel models, spreadsheets and reporting tools, helping create smarter and more efficient ways of working.
Who We're Looking For We're open to candidates at different stages of their career, but you'll likely bring:

  • A positive, can-do attitude and a proactive approach to getting things done.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to build strong relationships across the business.
  • High attention to detail and a commitment to accuracy.
  • 2–5 years' experience in an Assistant Management Accountant, Management Accountant, Assistant Accountant, Commercial Finance, Cost Accountant or Analyst role.
  • Experience supporting monthly management reporting, budgeting and forecasting processes.
  • Strong Excel skills, with the ability to develop and improve reporting models and dashboards.
  • A tertiary qualification in Accounting, Commerce or Finance.
  • CA/CPA qualification or active progression towards completion (not essential).
  • Exposure to costing, operational finance, manufacturing, industrial or supply chain environments will be highly regarded.
  • A commercial mindset with the ability to turn financial data into meaningful business insights.
  • Confidence working in a changing environment and contributing to continuous improvement initiatives.

Key Responsibilities

  • Assist with the preparation of monthly management accounts and reporting packs.
  • Support budgeting, forecasting and financial planning processes.
  • Analyse operational costs, including labour, inventory, overheads and other key business expenses.
  • Investigate variances and provide commentary on business performance.
  • Develop and enhance Excel models, reports and dashboards.
  • Support cash flow reporting and working capital analysis.
  • Partner with operational stakeholders to understand business performance and key cost drivers.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives across finance systems, processes and reporting.
  • Contribute to documenting and improving finance procedures and SOPs.

Most importantly, you’ll align with a values-led culture: collaborative, down-to-earth, and focused on doing right by people.

What’s on offer

  • A supportive, close-knit team within a respected WA business
  • South-of-the-river location, with 1 day working from home an flexibility after probation
  • Genuinely interesting, operational finance work with real business impact
  • The opportunity to influence systems, processes, and continuous improvement
  • A competitive salary of $80k–$100k + super DOE
  • A down-to-earth culture where your ideas and contribution will genuinely be valued

To apply, please click 'Apply' or contact Alisha at Hunter Manning for a confidential conversation.

job.title: Management Accountant
job.description:
Management Accountant | Make Your Mark in a Great Family Business
South of the River | Operational Finance | WA Business

We’re looking for someone with a great can-do attitude, strong communication skills, and a genuine willingness to roll up their sleeves and get involved. Someone who builds relationships easily, asks the right questions, and can turn numbers into clear, practical insights for the wider business.

Hunter Manning is partnering with a well-established Western Australian family business to find a Management Accountant who wants more than a number-crunching role. This is a business with genuine heart — a close-knit team, strong values, and a culture where people are known, supported, and encouraged to contribute ideas.

You won’t be a small cog in a large corporate machine; you’ll have real visibility, a voice, and the opportunity to make a tangible impact.

You’ll join a friendly, hands-on finance team and take ownership of month-end management reporting, costing, and operational analysis across the business.
Your work will go straight to the heart of the operation — analysing costs, inputs, performance, and key drivers, and helping leaders understand what’s driving results. No two days will look quite the same, and you’ll have plenty of scope to dig into interesting questions and provide insights that genuinely matter.

Be part of something bigger

With a system upgrade on the horizon, you’ll learn the business on its current systems first, then have a real say in shaping how the new system is set up.

  • Strong Excel skills is essential and genuine enjoyment in building and improving models

  • A curious mindset and a willingness to challenge “the way it’s always been done”
  • CA/CPA qualification, or study towards it (preferred, but not essential)
  • Exposure to operational, or fast-paced environment (a bonus, not a requirement)

Most importantly, you’ll align with a values-led culture: collaborative, down-to-earth, and focused on doing right by people.

What’s on offer

  • A supportive, close-knit team within a respected WA business
  • South-of-the-river location, with 1 day working from home an flexibility after probation
  • Genuinely interesting, operational finance work with real business impact
  • The opportunity to influence systems, processes, and continuous improvement
  • A competitive salary of $90k–$120k + super DOE
  • A down-to-earth culture where your ideas and contribution will genuinely be valued

To apply, please click 'Apply' or contact Jodie at Hunter Manning for a confidential conversation.
